Hope for farmers

By: Tarryn Crossman | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We meet two farmers who are doing everything they can to survive this drought and find out how one fb post can save 13 farms

Summary:
Synopsis
This is a story about two farmers from opposite sides of the country and how they are surviving the worst drought in years. It is a story about despair and hope, about community and the spirit of South Africans to survive. Oom Jim was emotional drained after having to mercy kill 4 of his cattle, not sure how he was going to see through the winter. As a last resort his daughter posted photo’s of the desperate situation on FB and South Africa responded in a way he could never have imagined.

Michris comes from generations of farmers that survived the droughts in ’96, but nothing could have prepared him for this past year. He has been documenting this drought for his son, so he will never forget, so that he will be more prepared if it ever happens again. Michris’s story is about despair, hope, community and a family living through the worst drought in years.

Further information:
Details
This piece tells the story of two farmers and how they are surviving the drought. It goes into their personal lives and tells a tale of anxiety, sleepless nights and emotional desperation. It also shows how these farmers love the land and as this drought cripples their community, South Africa is coming together to help them survive.

Michris was born into farming. He remembers his grandfather telling him about the drought in ’96 and how he should always have 2 months of food for his cattle. But over the last few months he has been photographing the drought for his son to show him that you need 5 months of food for them to survive, “we will never forget this drought” Michris
Having breakfast with his family and walking around his farm Michris tells us about the daily hell of trying to survive a drought. It is not only Michris and his family that are effected though, he has had to let go many of his casual workers. The whole community relies on the farmers to make living and therefore they are all affected by the decrease in income.

In pure desperation he planted sunflowers and maize in the dust a few weeks back. The community of farmers in the area gather for prayer sessions in the evenings, it was the day after one of these sessions that Michris got some rain. “God gave these sunflowers and maize a half a chance” Michris

With the rain come it allowed baby sprouts of grass to grow, which saved his sheep. But the cattle are so weak that the energy required to get at the short grass has taken the life of 4 of his cows this week alone.

But Michris is one of the lucky ones, because as his bore holes are drying up so he can dig new ones. For now. If the frost comes early and his maize is killed, then Michris loses and the drought wins. He will be bankrupt.




Oom Jim
Oom Jim has a commercial cattle farm in bray near the kalahari. They have had 60ml of rain since September 2015. He is a strong boer man, but the drought is getting the better of him. Waking up one morning he was told by the staff that some of the cattle couldn’t get up anymore. With tears in his eye Jim took his shot gun and killed 4 of his cattle, out of sheer mercy. His cows can’t be impregnated as they are too weak, so financially he is behind by 20 months and winter has not even arrived yet. Oom Jim is desperate and terrified for what winter is bringing. Feeling her fathers pain Nicolene posted some pictures on Facebook of the cows her father killed. The response from South Africa was over whelming. Nicole and her boyfriend have co-ordinated to get the the donations of hay bales and chicken waste to 13 farms in the Kalahari. Instead of trying to help a lot of farmers for one or two weeks, they have committed to helping these 13 farmers make it all the way through winter. The response from these strangers had Oom Jim in tears, “How do you say thank you to these people. How can I ever let them know how much they have done” Oom Jim

Press Release:


Farmers’ Hope
They watch their fertile land turn to desert in the devastating heat, forcing them to shoot starving cattle. Urban society bears the downstream consequences - food shortages and food price increases - but only farmers fully understand the gravity of the current drought and the relief that comes from any sign of hope. From the Kalahari to the Free State, Carte Blanche meets desperate farmers saved by ordinary people responding to social media calls to action.


Script:


Time code CHARACTER / VISUAL
1 00:00 Opening of the road and Michris with family praying Intro music

Michris: Dear Jesus, thank you for all the blessings that we have received, to be able to farm. Thank you for my children and wife. Give us rain. Bless us in this coming year. Amen .
2 00:19 Michris and windmill V/O: In the city we may have water restrictions be inconvenience in other small way

Derek Watts continue on screen: but we don’t really understand the drought like Mikless and Oom Jim, their eyes are always turned to the heavens.
3 00:34 Tree with road and cut to establishing of the farm V/O : Oom Jim Botha has been farming since he was 20 years old. In 2003 he moved his farm near Bray in the Kalahari.
4 00:46 Jim Botha I started farming in the 1980s, we are commercial cattle famers. The Kalahari is in your blood, the sand is in your blood, you caint remove it easily. Once you’ve fallen in love with the world , it’s the most wonderful world to live in.
5 01:05 Michris En Karlien, landscape with V/O Michris Janse van Rensburg they have been living on this farm near Bulfontein in the Freestate, for 15 years. On average they normally receive 300mil of rain per year but in 2015 they received less than 100.
6 01:23 Michris and Derek Watts interview Derek: When do you feel that this drought became a crisis?
Michris: When we starting to loose planting dates, you know as a farmer your handbook say your best time for planting is 20 November to 5th December for May. Every night when I see the date in the bible study book, 26 December and 27 December, 2nd of January I realize I didn’t plant yet.
7 01:56 Jim Botha We heard about the weather forecast and broadcasts said, El Nino is bad , we had it in the back of our minds we didn’t really believe it because the bible says ‘ Life and Death lies in the might of the tongue’ so if we believed it is going to be dry, then it will be dry. The Lord told us this, but if we believe it will rain then it will rain. So yes, it is all that we cling to.
8 02:43 Tractor with cows V/O : In a normal year between November and January Jims farm would receive an average 230mils of rain but with the same period during the drought they only receive 57mils.
9 02:55 Jim on a tracker moving bales to feed the cows and Madeline Both comments Jim: Okay…
Madeline : This is the last years bales that we have left we are going to surround everything we have for today. They just lie here then they wait for us to put out the bale because there is no more grass for them inside of the field

10 03:16 Madeline Botha speaks to camera with cows in the background So what happens is the stronger ones they eat first because they can push the weaker ones away so if we have more than one bale then we usually put out three or four but now we only have two left .
Five already died because they couldn’t even walk from the tree up to here where we feed them.
11 03:38 Jim Both Yah maybe one other time we must make a decision.
12 03:42 Madeline Botha speaks over images of cows feeding and some loosing weight. Jim Both joins as they look at the dying cows We caint keep on feeding because we don’t have any money left to feed them. Its bad seeing the weak ones dying in there. And you have to decide and its not their fault so if you have to decide (cries) that’s what makes it difficult because who do you help? Do you help your strong cows or do you help the weak ones? Which one do you help?
13 04:28 Jim Botha Our problem now is finding food for our animals but that’s not where it ends. My biggest worry is here on my farm I haven’t been able to put bulls with my cows because my cows are too weak for breeding. Every year Novemeber, I make my biggest sales when you farm bond has to be repaid . Now there wont be any calves. So how will I keep my responsibilities? If I have to loose all the cattle on the farm, how do u employ my workers? I don’t have an income to pay them, I’ll have to retrench them
14 05:14 Michris In December, normally it looks like England this year December it look like Afghanistan. Even our insurance they have specific dates where your maize must be germinated to pay out insurance and to pay out loans so we must have totalling.
15 05:36 Michris tendering the land V/O: Michris primary source of income is maize and on the 15th of January he got just enough rain to make him brave enough to plan his first crop almost one month late.
16 05:49 Michris and Derek speaking on the field Derek: Now this maize should be a lot higher by now hey?
Michris: Yeah No hey by this time of the year should be more higher…
Derek: up here…
Michris: higher
Derek: Michris if you look at your total maize production that you can expect this year what you recon you have percentage wise compared to previous years ?
Michris: uhm 20%
Derek: and would that be a reflection of the countries production 20%?
Michris: Yah I think so, of course we are late the percentage is even less.
17 06:20 Derek and Michris peaking Derek: sometimes I think us city people don’t really understand drought
Michris: this drought put a dentch onto the farmer and we are grateful to our families and friend even from people we don’t even know who support us.

You know Derek I still crying if I remember the day a friend from Eliot some friends they phoned me and said they gonna send me whole truck full of forum and maize and it cost them a lot. I don’t think we would’ve survived without their support.
18 : Jim Botha Now in January month, my daughter told me “dad you have to come and look it is getting worse. There are cows that just lie down that caint get up anymore” and then I came home and I got my gun and I told her I caint see them suffer anymore and then I shad to shoot 3 cows. When I turned around with the gun, then I left something broke then I heard poor Madeline started to cry in the house.
19 07:44 Oom jim and family walking through the gate. Facebook pictures V/O: Oom Jim’s other daughter from Johannesburg Nicolene and her partner Jaun saw the photos of her fathers farm and as a last resort posted them to facebook and asked for people to pray for her dad.
20 07:59 Madeline speaking to camera And after a while she phoned me and she said I’ve got such big reaction people are sharing it with each other and they want to send you water and they want to send you some grass that they cut from their grass in their city
21 08:13 Nicolene They were asking where is this farm and how can they help? we need water and stuff like that. And we obviously do need water but we need rain so I said we do need food for the animals then Juan stepped into all of this
22 08:31 Juan We decided to see theser famers oin a seven month plan so that we can get enough food for them to feed I think 3014 cattle in total.
23 08:42 Madeline We identified the 13 farmers that had the least rain and or aim is to help them first
24 08:42 Truck with maize driving down a hill and entering farms Music

V/O: South Africans from all over immediately came forward to help these 13 farmers and within two days, trucks arrived with 60 tons of chicken manure to give immediate relief.

25 09:07 Oom Jim with handling chicken manure from delivered from the trucks Alone we wont be able to overcome this drought. There are people that listen and there are people that care. I don’t know how will you ever replay the people offering help and providing help, how will you ever thank them? I don’t know… A ‘thank you’ is just too small I wish I could do more, but I caint. The only thing I can do is say ‘ Thank you’ .
26 09:47 Michris I think most farmers are scared that one day they are not going to be farmers and family… one day the 2015 drought destroyed us . so we help.
